contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you planned a sunlight investigation. Today, use the same fair-test idea to investigate water!

Same fair-test rule as yesterday: change only one thing. To test if plants need water, you'd use two of the same kind of plant, both getting the same sunlight — but one gets watered regularly and the other gets no water at all. Plan this investigation: what's the one thing that's different between your two plants this time? What do you predict will happen to the plant that gets no water?
You just planned a second real investigation, this time testing water! Tomorrow we'll learn something new: how animals actually help plants grow.

objectives: Apply the fair-test method to a new variable: water
Predict what happens to a plant deprived of water, based on real-world observation
materialsNeeded: Two same-type plants or seedlings, if available (optional but ideal)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's sunlight-investigation plan.
2. Introduce today's water investigation, using the same fair-test structure.
3. Have the child describe their own version of the plan on the worksheet.
4. If real plants are available, set this investigation up too.
5. Preview tomorrow's animal-and-plant lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: connect to a real memory — has the child ever seen a plant wilt from not being watered?
Ready for more: ask what would happen if BOTH sunlight and water were changed at once, and why that would no longer be a fair test
Reusing yesterday's exact structure (just swapping the variable) reinforces that this is a repeatable method, not a one-time trick
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an investigation-planning activity — check that the child identifies water as the one changed variable this time, with everything else kept the same, and predicts the unwatered plant will wilt or not grow well.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 2 Life Science standard 2-LS2-1 (plants need sunlight and water to grow), continuing this week's real scientific-investigation methodology with a second variable.

prompts.prompt: What is the one thing that's different between your two plants?
What do you predict will happen to the plant with no water?
